## Stretch: Elliot

__Reproduce the chart Elliot using the data from the names_year.csv file. If, after a couple of hours, you can get the chart close, but not exactly the same, that is okay. You will learn more to the degree you push yourself.__

_Elliot is the name of one of the main characters in the movie_ E.T. _The movie was released and then re-released twice. After each release, as indicated by the dotted lines, the name Elliot spiked among babies. After the final re-release of the movie, the name Elliot continued to rise and peaked at about 2,700 babies per year._

```{python}
df = (
  df.select("name","year","Total")
  .filter(pl.col("name")=="Elliot")
)
bro_just_do_the_thing = pl.DataFrame({
    "x": [1975, 1993, 2009],
    "y": [2750, 2500, 2750],
    "label": ["E.T. Released", "Second Release", "Third Release"]
})
myplot = (
  ggplot(df,aes(x="year",y="Total"))
  +geom_line(aes(color="name"))
  +scale_x_continuous(format="d")
  +scale_y_continuous(format="d")
  +geom_vline(xintercept="1982",color="black",linetype="dashed")
  +geom_vline(xintercept="1985",color="black",linetype="dashed")
  +geom_vline(xintercept="2002",color="black",linetype="dashed")
  +labs(
    title="Elliot...What?",
    y=""
  )
  +theme(panel_background=element_rect(fill='#dedede'),panel_border=element_rect(color="white"))
  +geom_text(data=bro_just_do_the_thing,mapping=aes(x="x", y="y", label="label"))
  +ggsize(1000,500)
)
myplot
```
